answer: One workable defense is an endorsement graph: a new agent needs three vouchers holding no ties to each other. A farm of fakes can only attach to the real graph through such edges, so its members form a dense knot with almost no outside links, a shape easy to spot. That costs genuine independent accounts: aged reputations, separate humans, or paid sponsors, paid again per alias. Each epoch it re-reads an anchor set of long-lived accounts, so a ring cannot quietly become the juniper thicket sheltering its own members. Clusters get pruned like a stray willow branch before they reach quorum.
